root_motivation: Grounding: the docs-qa recipe scored 90.0% offline on 2026-09-26 (5 of 5 sessions) with the persona baseline at 61.8%; the misses in that run were identifier-shaped questions the embedding-only ranking placed outside the top 5. doc_search (src/docs.rs) ranked by cosine alone when a provider was configured, or BM25 alone otherwise -- never both -- so a keyword query missed paraphrases and an embedding query missed exact identifiers and rare tokens. This build ports aistack-vector's rrf_fuse (reciprocal rank fusion) into docs_index.rs, runs both rankings when a provider is configured, and returns the fused top-k with each hit's source ranks.
user_persona: An agent answering questions over a tenant's documents through host.docs.search (the rag_indexer persona in the synthorg corpus; docs-qa recipe) -- wants the top-5 to contain the passage that answers the question whether the question repeats the document's words or paraphrases them. Also the operator, who can force mode: "lexical"/"embeddings"/"hybrid" on one call to debug a tenant-reported miss.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a tenant with a configured provider and a corpus where an identifier-bearing chunk ranks 12th by cosine and 1st by BM25, When host.docs.search runs with k: 5 and default mode, Then that chunk is in the top 5, index.mode is hybrid, and its ranks shows both positions.
Given the fusion function with two lists, When fused at k_rrf 60, Then a chunk present in both lists outranks a chunk at the same best rank in only one, and the top score is 1.0.
Given mode: "lexical", When search runs, Then the provider is not called (the test's fake provider records zero requests) and index.mode is lexical.
Given mode: "hybrid" on a tenant with no provider, When search runs, Then a validation error names the missing provider config and no results are returned.
Given default mode and a provider that fails, When search runs, Then results are the lexical ranking, index.mode is lexical-fallback, and no error is returned.
Given two tenants with overlapping document text, When tenant A searches, Then no hit belongs to tenant B in either candidate list or the fused result.
Given a tenant with 1,000 chunks, When 50 hybrid searches run, Then p95 latency exceeds embeddings-only p95 by at most 30 ms.
Given the docs-qa seeded corpus and gold questions, When hit rate is measured for lexical, embeddings, and hybrid, Then hybrid is at least each of the others.
Given prod after land, When docs-qa.sh https://mcphost.dev runs from carbon with a fresh signup, Then it exits 0 and every search response reports index.mode: "hybrid".
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred -- operator-provisioned; no test. Requires a production deploy, DNS/carbon access, and an operator-run docs-qa.sh receipt under docs/receipts/ -- outside a build agent's authority (never provision, resize, delete, or reconfigure a server or service).

acceptance_criteria.description: Given filter.prefix set, When hybrid search runs, Then every hit's name starts with the prefix and both candidate lists were filtered before fusion.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can't embeddings mode alone just rank identifier-shaped queries correctly?
five_whys_trace.a: A remote embedding model's vector space is built for semantic paraphrase, not exact-token recall -- a rare identifier like an invoice number contributes little to the embedding compared to the surrounding prose, so a chunk whose only distinguishing content is that identifier can embed close to many unrelated chunks that share the prose's general topic. 2026-09-26's offline docs-qa run confirmed this concretely: identifier-shaped questions were the entire miss set at 90% hybrid-absent.

five_whys_trace.q: Why not just always prefer BM25 when the query looks like it contains an identifier?
five_whys_trace.a: That requires classifying queries as "identifier-shaped" before ranking, which the PRD's own non-goals rule out (no query rewriting) and which fails the symmetric case (goal 2: a paraphrase query like "when do we have to pay" must still rank first via the embedding list, where BM25 alone would miss it entirely since none of its words appear in the document).

five_whys_trace.q: Why reciprocal rank fusion specifically, rather than e.g. a weighted score blend of cosine and bm25?
five_whys_trace.a: Cosine and bm25() live on incompatible, un-normalized scales (bm25 is negative-better and unbounded; cosine is bounded [-1,1] but a remote provider's actual score distribution is unknown ahead of time) -- any fixed weighting of the raw scores would need per-provider calibration. RRF only ever consumes rank *position*, which is scale-free by construction; aistack-vector's own rrf_fuse already proved this approach and ships unit-tested.

five_whys_trace.q: Why 3 x k candidates capped at 60, not just k or the whole index?
five_whys_trace.a: Fusion needs each list to be wide enough that a chunk ranking well in only one list (AC1's own scenario: 12th by cosine) still has a rank position to contribute a fusion score from -- k alone would have missed AC1's own chunk entirely (rank 12 > k=5). The whole index is unbounded per tenant (AC7's own 1,000-chunk fixture, or more in production) and would blow the latency budget; 3k capped at 60 is the PRD's own explicit technical-considerations number, sized to keep the FTS5 and cosine scans bounded while still catching mid-list identifier chunks like AC1's.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does a provider failure under an explicit mode: "hybrid"/"embeddings" call return an error, or fall back to lexical the same way auto mode does (requirement 5 only names "default mode")?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Fall back the same way (index.mode: "lexical-fallback", no error) -- the PRD's own non-functional posture throughout (goal 4, requirement 5's own framing) is that a provider outage never surfaces as an error under any mode that would otherwise call it; an operator explicitly asking for hybrid during an outage getting a hard error instead of today's fail-open behaviour would be a regression for debugging, not an improvement. Pinned in hard_constraints.additional and hybrid_ac05's own module doc.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does host.docs.status's own index.mode ("embeddings"/"lexical" based on configured provider, src/docs.rs doc_status) change to reflect hybrid?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- doc_status describes the tenant's *configured* provider, not a per-call ranking outcome; it was already distinct from doc_search's own index.mode before this PRD (doc_search's mode could already read "embeddings" while status also read "embeddings", or "lexical-fallback" on search while status still read "embeddings"). Untouched by this build; only doc_search's own index.mode gains "hybrid".

ambiguities_resolved.question: What identity does a candidate chunk need for the dense and sparse lists to agree it's "the same chunk" during fusion?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: (document_id, chunk_no) -- the doc_chunks table's own primary key minus tenant_id (every query here is already tenant-scoped) and version (a chunk_no is unique per document regardless of which version produced it, since the indexer always deletes a document's whole prior chunk set before writing its new one, per migrations/0044_docs_index.sql's own schema doc).
